comment: Curl port clients (https://github.com/StewartScottRogers/Curl) the extended servers' Integration tests may connect with, and Phase 7 measures beside pinned upstream curl, pinned by SHA-256 (ADR-0083 decision 2, ADR-0089). Never an oracle, never an expected value, never ADR evidence, and never a test client for an original protocol; never list an upstream curl build here, nor a port client in UpstreamCurlBuilds.json, and the two files never share a SHA-256. Each entry's kind is 'curl' (the port's curl executable, run as a command; an entry with no kind is a curl) or 'library' (the port's managed Libcurl assembly, compiled against and called only by Run-CurlPortLibcurlWebSocketScript.cs and Run-CurlPortLibcurlRtspScript.cs, never run as a curl; ADR-0089 decision 1 (c)); a library is pinned at the same commit as its curl. To add an entry: take a commit of the port's master into a folder outside both repositories (for example 'git archive <commit>' from a clone, so no working tree is disturbed), publish its curl executable ('dotnet publish Curl.Console -c Release -r win-x64 -o %LOCALAPPDATA%\Surl\curl-port\<commit>') or its Libcurl assembly ('dotnet publish Libcurl -c Release -o %LOCALAPPDATA%\Surl\curl-port\<commit>\libcurl') under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Surl\curl-port\<commit>\ on Windows (%HOME%/.local/share/surl/curl-port/<commit>/ elsewhere), then add {platform, path, sha256, commit, publishCommand, published} and, for a library, kind. A path may name environment variables as %NAME%; they are expanded when the client is located. Re-pinning is an ordinary commit, not an ADR.

builds.publishCommand: git archive b42c319ba940f66452b2b6f3e9910d46825b08fe | tar -x -C "C:\Users\Stewart Rogers\AppData\Local\Surl\curl-port-source\b42c319ba940f66452b2b6f3e9910d46825b08fe", then in that folder: dotnet publish Libcurl -c Release -o "C:\Users\Stewart Rogers\AppData\Local\Surl\curl-port\b42c319ba940f66452b2b6f3e9910d46825b08fe\libcurl"
